Website design for US local businesses

Restaurant website design.

People often visit a restaurant website with a simple decision to make: what to eat, when to come, and how to arrange a table. We design restaurant and café websites that make that information easy to find on a phone, with space for your food, atmosphere, and private-dining options.

Talk about your website

Make the menu readable on a phone.

Menu sections should use readable text, with dish names, descriptions, and prices supplied by your business. An image-only menu can make browsing harder, especially when someone has to pinch and zoom. State when menus are seasonal and explain how customers can ask about dietary requirements. Allergen information should come from your kitchen and reflect your actual procedures.

Answer the practical visiting questions.

Publish accurate opening hours, location, directions, accessibility information, and contact options. Explain walk-ins, table requests, party-size limits, and any confirmed booking rules. A customer should be able to distinguish a request from a confirmed reservation. Holiday hours and changing menus need an agreed updating process so the website stays useful after launch.

Give private dining its own conversation.

Group bookings may need the occasion, preferred date, guest count, and space requirements. A dedicated page can explain the kind of gatherings you accommodate, how to inquire, and when a team member will discuss availability or menu options. Minimum spend, deposits, and cancellation terms should reflect your actual arrangements rather than generic promises.

Connect the website to your service style.

Use photography that reflects the dining experience and copy that sounds like your restaurant. We can plan inquiry acknowledgments for group events and review requests after an agreed customer interaction. If you use a reservation or ordering provider, its compatibility, fees, and integration scope are discussed before agreement. The website package does not automatically include an ordering platform.

Pages worth planning.

We choose your 10–20 pages together. A starting point for restaurants:

  • Food menu
  • Drinks
  • Restaurant story
  • Private dining
  • Visit information
  • Table requests and dining questions

Restaurants website questions.

Will the restaurant menu be readable without downloading a PDF?

The menu can be presented as ordinary web content with sections and clear text so visitors can read it directly on their phones. You supply the current menu and prices, and we agree on how future changes will be handled.

Does the package include restaurant reservations or online ordering?

We discuss the reservation or ordering system you use and the contact path the website needs. Third-party integrations, fees, payments, and live availability are confirmed in scope. An inquiry form alone does not confirm a table or process an order.

Is Olive & Ember an actual restaurant client?

No. It is a fictional restaurant website created to demonstrate our design approach. Its menu, story, and request forms are illustrative. Your restaurant website would use your own verified business information and approved content.
